To determine the sharp threshold $\alpha_{\mathrm{dom}}^\star$ as a function of the committee size $k$, consider the geometry of voter preferences in the canonical impartial culture model as the number of candidates $m \to \infty$ for a sufficiently large fixed number of voters $n$.

In this setting, the normalized rank profiles of candidates across the $n$ voters asymptotically become uniformly distributed over $[0, 1]^n$. For any chosen committee $S$ of size $k$ and any candidate $a \notin S$, the relative rankings of $S \cup \{a\}$ across voters define the fraction of voters who prefer individual members $b \in S$ to $a$. 

By constructing the committee $S$ to optimally cover the voter space and analyzing the worst-case adversarial candidate $a \notin S$ that minimizes $\max_{b \in S} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{I}(b \succ_i a)$, the limiting minimax value achieves the sharp threshold of:
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{dom}}^\star = \frac{k}{k+1}$$

For any $\alpha < \frac{k}{k+1}$, an $\alpha$-dominating set of size $k$ exists with probability approaching $1$ as $m \to \infty$, whereas for any $\alpha > \frac{k}{k+1}$, the probability approaches $0$.

ANSWER: \frac{k}{k+1}
